fix_commit.message: Avoid unsigned integer overflow in the delta_apply() extension function. Not part of any standard deliverable. [forum:/forumpost/d41879b367c7f7ec|Forum thread d41879b367c7f7ec].
fix_commit.author: drh

findings.title: Unsigned 32-bit integer overflow in delta_apply() allows buffer overflow
findings.message: In delta_apply(), the variables `limit` and `total` are declared as `unsigned int` (32-bit on most platforms). `limit` is populated from a caller-controlled delta header via deltaGetInt(), and `total` accumulates byte counts (also `unsigned int`) from copy ('@') and insert (':') delta operations. If a malicious delta blob encodes a large `limit` value and supplies copy/insert operations whose `cnt` values collectively sum beyond UINT_MAX (4,294,967,295), `total` wraps around to a small value due to unsigned 32-bit overflow. The guard `if( total > limit )` then passes incorrectly, allowing subsequent memcpy() calls to write past the end of the pre-allocated `zOut` output buffer, resulting in a heap buffer overflow.
findings.suggestion: Widen both `limit` and `total` to a 64-bit unsigned integer type (sqlite3_uint64) so that accumulation of byte counts cannot wrap around for any practical input size. This matches the fix applied in commit 9a341c1edbde.

ground_truth.root_cause: The `total` accumulator and `limit` bound were both typed as `unsigned int` (32-bit), which wraps silently on overflow. Since both values originate from attacker-controlled delta data parsed by deltaGetInt(), a malicious input can trigger wrap-around of `total` so it appears smaller than `limit`, defeating the intended bounds check.
